title: Gradient boosting predicts Pseudomonas syringae virulence on bean from genome k-mers
summary: Virulence of 121 diverse P. syringae isolates on common bean was measured in a rapid seed infection assay, and bean isolates were more virulent on bean than non-bean isolates. Gradient boosting trained on whole-genome k-mers predicted virulence with a mean absolute error of 0.05. For 16 strains whose virulence was predicted, 15 (94%) had measured virulence within the predicted bounds. The study covers one pathogen-host system and is described as a proof of principle.
ai_technology: Gradient boosting machine learning on whole-genome k-mers, type III effector k-mers and effector/phytotoxin presence-absence to predict strain virulence on bean
organization: Department of Cell & Systems Biology, University of Toronto

evidence.tested: Virulence of 121 isolates measured on bean; model predictions for 16 strains checked experimentally, 15 within bounds.
evidence.unknown: Whether the approach transfers to other hosts or pathogens; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Gradient boosted decision trees predicting strain virulence from genomic features
